end.summary:
Practised drawing dot pictures for square and triangular numbers.
Used rows and columns to represent 4×4, 5×5, and 12×12 squares.
Showed that the shared corner is counted once when adding a row and column.
Used an L-shaped picture to explain 25−16=9 and the odd-number growth pattern.
Applied the method to move from 6×6 to 7×7 using 13 added coins.
end.parentNote: Ishita practised representing square numbers with dot pictures and explaining how one square grows to the next. They used the shared-corner idea to avoid double-counting and correctly explained the 16-to-25 jump as adding 9 dots. At one point the new square’s dimensions were unclear, but this was corrected by using an L-shaped row-and-column picture; at the end, they applied the method to 6×6 to 7×7. At home, ask them to draw 3×3, 4×4, and 5×5 squares and circle the new L-shape each time.
